hindi: सन्धि और विग्रह में वृद्धि समान होने पर सन्धि को अपनाए।
english: In peace and war, when growth is equal, [one] should adopt peace.
notes: sandhi = peace (as in 8.5/9.7/12.5), vigraha = war. upeyāt (upa-√i) is literally 'should approach'; 'adopt' is the natural sense with sandhi. The subject is unstated, so '[one]'. The locative dual of the dvandva is read as 'in (the two) peace and war'.

words.gloss: loss, expenditure, absence from home, obstacles

hindi: क्योंकि विग्रह में क्षय, व्यय, प्रवास, बाधाएँ होती हैं।
english: For in war there are loss, expenditure, absence from home and obstacles.
notes: pravāsa = sojourn away from home (abroad). pratyavāya is rendered 'obstacles' (alternatives: mishap, detriment, adverse consequence); the exact sense is not fully certain.

hindi: इससे आसन और यान में से आसन की व्याख्या की गई।
english: By that, among staying quiet and marching, staying quiet is explained.
notes: Formula 'tena X vyākhyātam' (glossary). The genitive dual āsana-yānayoḥ is read as partitive 'among the two'. yāna = marching (going out against an enemy); Hindi keeps यान as the technical term. What 'tena' refers back to is not stated in the unit.

words.gloss: the dual policy and seeking shelter

hindi: द्वैधीभाव और संश्रय में से द्वैधीभाव को अपनाए।
english: Among the dual policy and seeking shelter, [one] should adopt the dual policy.
notes: gacchet with an accusative is literally 'should go to'; 'adopt' as in unit 1. The dual genitive/locative is read as partitive 'among the two'. saṃśraya = seeking shelter (with a stronger king).

words.gloss: having his own action as chief

hindi: क्योंकि द्वैधीभूत, अपने कर्म को प्रधान रखने वाला, अपना ही उपकार करता है, किन्तु संश्रित दूसरे का उपकार करता है, अपना नहीं।
english: For one who has become dual, having his own action as chief, does good only to himself, but one who has taken shelter does good to another, not to himself.
notes: 'ātmana' is ātmanaḥ (visarga lost before e). The genitive with upa-√kṛ is read as 'does good to'. karma = action per glossary; 'work' is possible. dvaidhī-bhūta = one who has taken the dual policy (literally 'become dual').
lines_deva: द्वैधी.भूतो हि स्व.कर्म.प्रधान आत्मन एव-उपकरोति, संश्रितस् तु परस्य-उपकरोति, न-आत्मनः
lines_iast: dvaidhī.bhūto hi sva.karma.pradhāna ātmana eva-upakaroti, saṃśritas tu parasya-upakaroti, na-ātmanaḥ

hindi: सामन्त जिस बल वाला है, उससे विशिष्ट बल वाले का आश्रय ले।
english: Of whatever force the neighbouring chief [is], [one] should resort to [one] of force superior to that.
notes: sāmanta = neighbouring chief (glossary 9.7). 'yad-balaḥ sāmantaḥ' is a relative clause without a verb; the copula is bracketed. 'tad-viśiṣṭa-bala' is read as bahuvrīhi 'whose force is superior to that', 'that' being the neighbouring chief's force.

words.gloss: in the absence of force superior to that

hindi: उससे विशिष्ट बल के अभाव में, उसी का आश्रय लेकर, कोश, सेना, भूमि में से किसी एक के द्वारा उसका उपकार करने के लिए अदृष्ट होकर प्रयत्न करे।
english: In the absence of [one of] force superior to that, having resorted to that very [one], [he] should try, unseen, to do good to him by any one of treasury, army and land.
notes: daṇḍa = army in the list of constituents (kośa, daṇḍa, bhūmi). 'tam' is read as the neighbouring chief of unit 6 (alternative: the stronger king just mentioned); asya likewise. adṛṣṭaḥ = literally 'unseen' (probably 'without being seen by him', i.e. not appearing in person); sense not certain. The genitive plural with anyatama is partitive 'any one of'.
lines_deva: तद्.विशिष्ट.बल.अभावे तम् एव-आश्रितः कोश.दण्ड.भूमीनाम् अन्यतमेन-अस्य-उपकर्तुम् अदृष्टः प्रयतेत
lines_iast: tad.viśiṣṭa.bala.abhāve tam eva-āśritaḥ kośa.daṇḍa.bhūmīnām anyatamena-asya-upakartum adṛṣṭaḥ prayateta

words.gloss: one at war with an enemy
words.gram: tat-puruṣa, m. abl. sg. ppp. vi-√grah

hindi: क्योंकि राजाओं के लिए विशिष्ट बल का समागम महान् दोष है, शत्रु से विग्रह में लगे हुए को छोड़कर।
english: For coming together with superior force [is] a great fault for kings, except [one] at war with an enemy.
notes: The copula is supplied (bracketed in English). anyatra takes the ablative: 'except [in the case of] one at war with an enemy'; vigṛhīta (vi-√grah) = engaged in war/hostility. 'ari' could be 'the (king's) enemy'. samāgama could also be 'union, alliance'.

words.gloss: like one submitting with his army

hindi: अशक्य होने पर सेना सहित समर्पण करने वाले के समान आचरण करे।
english: When [it is] impossible, [one] should behave like one submitting with his army.
notes: aśakye is a locative absolute without a noun ('in the impossible'); what is impossible is not stated (presumably the course of unit 8 or the earlier alternatives). daṇḍa-upanata follows the glossary (12.5).

words.gloss: on the pretext of plausible illness, dharma, business
words.gram: dvandva with attribute, m. inst. sg.

hindi: और जब इसके प्राणहारी रोग, भीतरी कोप, शत्रु की वृद्धि, मित्र का व्यसन या उपस्थित को, और उसके कारण वाली अपनी वृद्धि को देखे, तब विश्वसनीय रोग, धर्म, कार्य के बहाने से हट जाए।
english: And when [he] may see his life-taking disease, internal revolt, growth of an enemy, calamity of an ally, or [any such] arisen, and growth of himself caused by that, then [he] should withdraw on the pretext of a plausible illness, dharma and business.
notes: asya = the king he has taken shelter with. antaḥ-kopa = internal revolt (glossary 8.2). 'upasthitaṃ vā' is construed with the whole list ('or [any such] arisen'); alternatives: 'or at hand'. tan-nimittām: nimitta read as 'cause' (glossary's 'for the purpose of' does not fit a feminine adjective of vṛddhi); 'for the sake of that' is the alternative. sambhāvya (gerundive of sam-√bhū caus.) = 'to be thought possible, plausible'; it may qualify only vyādhi. The three pretexts form one dvandva (commas in Hindi). apadeśa = pretext (lit. pointing out). Alternative: upasthitam (n.) may agree with mitra-vyasanam ('an ally's calamity that has arisen'), and the vā may then join the last item ('or his own growth caused by that').
lines_deva: यदा च-अस्य प्राण.हरं व्याधिम् अन्तः.कोपं शत्रु.वृद्धिं मित्र.व्यसनम् उपस्थितं वा तन्.निमित्ताम् आत्मनश् च वृद्धिं पश्येत् तदा सम्भाव्य.व्याधि.धर्म.कार्य.अपदेशेन-अपयायात्
lines_iast: yadā ca-asya prāṇa.haraṃ vyādhim antaḥ.kopaṃ śatru.vṛddhiṃ mitra.vyasanam upasthitaṃ vā tan.nimittām ātmanaś ca vṛddhiṃ paśyet tadā sambhāvya.vyādhi.dharma.kārya.apadeśena-apayāyāt

hindi: या अपने देश में स्थित होकर पास न जाए।
english: Or, standing in [his] own territory, [he] should not approach [him].
notes: The object of upagacchet is not stated; '[him]' (the stronger king) is supplied in English only. viṣaya = territory (Hindi देश). -stha written without a dot in the e-text, as elsewhere in the book.

hindi: या समीप होकर इसके छिद्रों पर प्रहार करे।
english: Or, [being] near, [he] should strike at his weak points.
notes: 'cchidreṣu' is regular sandhi (doubling of ch after asya), not a typo. chidra = weak point (glossary 13.4). asya = the stronger king's (or the neighbour's); not specified.

hindi: या दो बलवानों के मध्य में गया हुआ, रक्षा करने में समर्थ का आश्रय ले, अथवा जिसका अन्तर्धि हो, अथवा दोनों का।
english: Or, gone to the middle of two stronger [ones], [he] should resort to [one] capable of protection, or [one] whose antardhi there may be, or both.
notes: antardhi is obscure: literally 'concealment, disappearance', here possibly an arrangement of hiding/sheltering or a person acting as a screen; kept untranslated, no sense guessed. Who is meant by 'yasya' is not clear. 'ubhau vā' = or [resort to] both. balīyasoḥ is genitive or locative dual ('of / between the two stronger').
lines_deva: बलीयसोर् वा मध्य.गतस् त्राण.समर्थम् आश्रयेत, यस्य वा-अन्तर्धिः स्यात्, उभौ वा
lines_iast: balīyasor vā madhya.gatas trāṇa.samartham āśrayeta, yasya vā-antardhiḥ syāt, ubhau vā

words.gloss: one who takes away the base

words.gram: pres. part. apa-√diś, m. nom. sg.

hindi: कपाल-संश्रय रहे, दूसरे के प्रति दूसरे को मूल हरने वाला बताता हुआ।
english: [He] should remain a kapāla-saṃśraya, pointing out the other to the other as one who takes away the base.
notes: kapāla-saṃśraya is obscure (kapāla = skull, potsherd, bowl) and kept untranslated; no sense guessed. mūla-hara is rendered literally ('taker of the base'; mūla = base, glossary 9.2); a technical sense (e.g. one who seizes the capital or root) is possible. 'itarasya itaram' is read as 'to the one, the other'; 'each to the other' is also possible. Alternative: itarasya taken with mūla-haram: 'pointing out the other as the taker of the other's base'; the genitive is not a true dative.

words.gloss: of the two who have split

hindi: या दोनों के परस्पर निर्देश वाले भेद का प्रयोग करे; भिन्न हुए दोनों का गुप्त दण्ड।
english: Or [he] should employ dissension of both, with mutual pointing-out; of the two who have split, secret punishment.
notes: The second clause has no verb; prayuñjīta is understood, but nothing is supplied in the translations. daṇḍa = punishment (upāṃśu-daṇḍa = secret punishment, glossary 13.5). paraspara-apadeśam agrees with bhedam ('dissension having mutual pointing-out / mutual pretexts'); apadeśa is 'pretext, pointing out' (as in units 10 and 14). 'ubhayoḥ' could also be 'between both'.
lines_deva: भेदम् उभयोर् वा परस्पर.अपदेशं प्रयुञ्जीत, भिन्नयोर् उपांशु.दण्डम्
lines_iast: bhedam ubhayor vā paraspara.apadeśaṃ prayuñjīta, bhinnayor upāṃśu.daṇḍam

hindi: या बल में स्थित दोनों के पार्श्व में स्थित होकर आसन्न भय से प्रतिकार करे।
english: Or, standing at the side of two established in strength, [he] should counteract from imminent fear.
notes: Uncertain construction. āsanna-bhaya could be 'fear that is near' or 'fear of the near one' (i.e. counteract the one from whom danger is near); the ablative may be of cause or of source. balastha = standing in strength (powerful, or stationed with an army). pratikurvīta has no stated object.

hindi: या दुर्ग के आश्रय वाला द्वैधीभूत रहे।
english: Or, having a fort as refuge, having become dual, [he] should remain.
notes: dvaidhī-bhūta as in unit 5 (one who has taken the dual policy). durga = fort (glossary).

words.gloss: by the causes of the sequence of peace and war

hindi: या सन्धि और विग्रह के क्रम के हेतुओं से चेष्टा करे।
english: Or [he] should act by the causes of the sequence of peace and war.
notes: The compound can also be a dvandva of four: 'by peace, war, sequence and causes'. The tat-puruṣa reading is chosen. hetu could also be 'reasons, grounds'.

hindi: दोनों के दूष्यों, शत्रुओं, आटविकों को सहारा दे।
english: [He] should support the treasonable, enemies and forest chiefs of both.
notes: dūṣya = the treasonable, āṭavika = forest chief (glossary). upa-√grah follows the glossary (support); 'seize, win over' are possible. Hindi gives the three-member dvandva with commas only.

hindi: इन दोनों में से एक के पास जाता हुआ, उन्हीं के द्वारा दूसरे के व्यसन में प्रहार करे।
english: Going to one of these two, [he] should strike, by those very [ones], in the calamity of the other.
notes: 'taiḥ' refers to the dūṣya, amitra and āṭavika of unit 19. anyatara is 'one of two'; the second occurrence is taken as 'the other'. vyasana = calamity (glossary).
lines_deva: एतयोर् अन्यतरं गच्छंस् तैर् एव-अन्यतरस्य व्यसने प्रहरेत्
lines_iast: etayor anyataraṃ gacchaṃs tair eva-anyatarasya vyasane praharet

hindi: या दो से आहत होकर मण्डल को आश्रय बनाकर रहे, मध्यम या उदासीन का संश्रय ले।
english: Or, harmed by two, [he] should remain having the circle as refuge; [he] should take shelter with the middle king or the neutral king.
notes: maṇḍala = circle (glossary 6.2); 'having the circle as refuge' is kept literal. upahata = struck, harmed, afflicted. The second vā joins madhyama and udāsīna.
lines_deva: द्वाभ्याम् उपहतो वा मण्डल.अपाश्रयस् तिष्ठेत्, मध्यमम् उदासीनं वा संश्रयेत
lines_iast: dvābhyām upahato vā maṇḍala.apāśrayas tiṣṭhet, madhyamam udāsīnaṃ vā saṃśrayeta

hindi: उसके साथ एक को सहारा देकर दूसरे का उच्छेद करे, अथवा दोनों का।
english: Together with him, having supported one, [he] should cut off the other, or both.
notes: 'tena' refers to the middle or neutral king of unit 21. ucchid = cut off, uproot, destroy.
lines_deva: तेन सह-एकम् उपगृह्य-इतरम् उच्छिन्द्याद्, उभौ वा
lines_iast: tena saha-ekam upagṛhya-itaram ucchindyād, ubhau vā

words.gloss: of the middle [king] and the neutral [king]

hindi: या दो से उच्छिन्न होकर मध्यम और उदासीन की, या उनके पक्ष के राजाओं की न्याय-वृत्ति का आश्रय ले।
english: Or, cut off by two, [he] should resort to the just conduct of the middle king and the neutral king, or of kings belonging to their party.

text_flags.why: possible typo: the book writes madhyama.udāsīna elsewhere and unit 21 has madhyamam udāsīnam

notes: nyāya-vṛtti is rendered 'just conduct'; it may also be 'a course of lawful livelihood / dependence'. The genitives are taken with nyāya-vṛttim. 'madhya' is taken as madhyama (see text_flags).
lines_deva: द्वाभ्याम् उच्छिन्नो वा मध्यम.उदासीनयोस् तत्.पक्षीयाणां वा राज्ञां न्याय.वृत्तिम् आश्रयेत
lines_iast: dvābhyām ucchinno vā madhyama.udāsīnayos tat.pakṣīyāṇāṃ vā rājñāṃ nyāya.vṛttim āśrayeta

hindi: या समानों में से जिसकी प्रकृतियाँ इसमें सुख पाएँ; या जहाँ स्थित होकर अपना उद्धार कर सके; या जहाँ पूर्वजों के योग्य गति या निकट का सम्बन्ध हो, मित्र अधिक या अति शक्तिशाली हों।
english: Or, among equals, [the one] whose constituent elements would find pleasure in him; or, standing where, [he] could rescue himself; or where [there is] a course fit for ancestors, or a near connection, [or where] allies would be more numerous or very powerful.
notes: A list of alternative choices with no main verb of its own; it continues the 'resort to' of units 21-23 and leads to unit 25. sukhyeyuḥ is a denominative of sukha; 'would find pleasure in' (alternative: 'would be happy with'); enam = the one seeking shelter. prakṛti = constituent elements (glossary). 'pūrva-puruṣa' = ancestors (literally 'former men'). The last clause is read as 'allies would be more numerous or very powerful'; its link with the preceding yatra clause is uncertain. bhūyāṃsi is the comparative 'more', no noun 'numerous' stated.
lines_deva: तुल्यानां वा यस्य प्रकृतयः सुख्येयुर् एनम्, यत्रस्थो वा शक्नुयाद् आत्मानम् उद्धर्तुम्, यत्र वा पूर्व.पुरुष.उचिता गतिर् आसन्नः सम्बन्धो वा, मित्राणि भूयांस्य् अतिशक्तिमन्ति वा भवेयुः
lines_iast: tulyānāṃ vā yasya prakṛtayaḥ sukhyeyur enam, yatrastho vā śaknuyād ātmānam uddhartum, yatra vā pūrva.puruṣa.ucitā gatir āsannaḥ sambandho vā, mitrāṇi bhūyāṃsy atiśaktimanti vā bhaveyuḥ

hindi: प्रिय जिसका हो, अथवा जो इसका प्रिय हो, उन दोनों में कौन? जिसका प्रिय हो, वह उसके पास जाए। यह आश्रय की परम गति है।
english: Dear to whom [he] would be, or who is dear to him: which of the two? [He who is] dear to whom, he should go to him. Such is the highest course of refuge.
notes: The pronoun references are ambiguous and the sense is uncertain: the second line is read as 'the one who is dear to X should go to X'. Alternative: the reverse (go to the one dear to oneself). The closing 'iti' opens the summing-up label 'Such is the highest course of refuge' (glossary). A verse (anuṣṭubh) of two lines of 16 syllables.
lines_deva: प्रियो यस्य भवेद् यो वा प्रियो ऽस्य कतरस् तयोः
प्रियो यस्य स तं गच्छेद् इत्य् आश्रय.गतिः परा
lines_iast: priyo yasya bhaved yo vā priyo 'sya kataras tayoḥ
priyo yasya sa taṃ gacched ity āśraya.gatiḥ parā
